title: Tailwind v4 CLI auto-scans the whole project for candidate classes by default
cause: Without an explicit source configuration, @import "tailwindcss" makes the CLI heuristically scan every file in the project (respecting .gitignore) for strings that look like Tailwind classes and compiles CSS for them - including string literals inside Python test files/docstrings, not just template/JS files.
fix: Use @import "tailwindcss" source(none); plus an explicit @source pointing only at the intended content file(s). Verified: a security-test string "bg-[url(evil)]" in a pytest file got compiled into the output before source(none) was added; confirmed absent after.

title: Debian bookworm's apt nodejs package is too old for Tailwind v4
cause: apt-cache policy nodejs on the ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm-slim image resolves to 18.20.4, but Tailwind v4 (@tailwindcss/cli) requires Node 20+.
fix: Install Node 20 from NodeSource in the Docker builder stage (curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - && apt-get install -y nodejs) instead of apt's default nodejs package. The base image also lacks curl/ca-certificates/gnupg - install those first.

title: Tailwind v4's default color palette renders as oklch(), not rgb()
cause: Tailwind v4 switched its default color palette to the OKLCH color space. getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor for a class like bg-blue-500 returns "oklch(0.623 0.214 259.815)", not an rgb(...) string.
fix: When asserting on computed colors in browser tests (Playwright etc.) against Tailwind v4 output, expect oklch(...) strings, not rgb(...). Verified via a real Playwright run against a live editor page.

title: tests/test_ai_transform.py's happy-path test hits the real configured AI_PROVIDER, not a fake
error_message: KeyError: 'done'
cause: test_valid_request_returns_operations doesn't mock EditorAIService.stream_generate_operations, so it goes through to whatever AI_PROVIDER is set in .env (e.g. opencode_zen, a real live model) - the model occasionally proposes something the server-side validator rejects (invalid_operations), which is expected AI-output variance, not a code bug. This makes the test flaky in any environment where .env configures a real provider.
fix: Don't treat this test's occasional failure as a regression signal without first checking the actual rejection reason (views.py's invalid_operations log now includes it, see the wizard_service.py precedent for that pattern). To make this test deterministic, mock the provider like every other test in the file already does.

title: Django collectstatic/WhiteNoise post-processing fails on build-source CSS files inside STATICFILES_DIRS
error_message: whitenoise.storage.MissingFileError: The file 'editor/tailwindcss' could not be found
cause: CompressedManifestStaticFilesStorage post-processes every collected CSS file looking for relative url()/@import references to rewrite. A Tailwind build-source file (tailwind-input.css, containing @import "tailwindcss") sitting inside STATICFILES_DIRS gets treated as a real static asset and fails post-processing since "tailwindcss" isn't a real relative file.
fix: Exclude build-source files from collectstatic with --ignore=<filename> (e.g. --ignore=tailwind-input.css --ignore=.tailwind-safelist.txt) - they're compiled into a real output file (tailwind.css) that IS meant to be collected normally.

title: DRF BooleanField treats an absent key as False for multipart/form data, not the model default
cause: DRF's BooleanField has HTML-checkbox-convention handling: for multipart/form-encoded requests, an absent boolean field is coerced to False (mimicking an unchecked HTML checkbox) instead of being omitted from validated_data (which is what happens for a plain JSON request, letting the model's own default apply). A product-creation form that uploads a file (forcing multipart) silently created every product as is_active=False even though the model default is True and the field was never touched.
fix: Declare the field explicitly with an explicit default on the serializer (e.g. is_active = serializers.BooleanField(required=False, default=True)) instead of relying on ModelSerializer's auto-generated field + the model's own default=True. Only bites when the request uses multipart/form-data (e.g. because of an accompanying file upload) - a pure JSON POST to the same endpoint does not trigger it, which is why it's easy to miss in JSON-only tests.

title: Stripe webhook signature verification works fully offline, no network needed
cause: stripe.Webhook.construct_event(payload, sig_header, webhook_secret) performs a local HMAC computation against the raw payload and webhook_secret - it never calls the Stripe API. This means signature-rejection behavior can be unit-tested directly (a bogus sig_header against any secret_key raises stripe.error.SignatureVerificationError) without any real API key, test-mode or otherwise.
fix: Test the invalid-signature rejection path directly against StripePaymentProvider.parse_webhook_event with a fake secret_key/sig_header - no need to skip this test or gate it behind real Stripe credentials.

title: Tailwind max-w-* has a named container-width scale separate from the numeric spacing scale
error_message: AI produced invalid operations for user 40: disallowed Tailwind class: max-w-4xl
cause: apps/ai_assistant/tailwind_classes.py's UTILITY_FAMILIES only mapped max-w to SIZING_SCALE (the numeric px/rem-based scale shared with w/h/min-w/etc), but Tailwind's max-w-* utility also has its own named scale (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl..7xl, full, min, max, fit, prose, none) used for page/content containers. max-w-4xl is one of the most common Tailwind classes for a page wrapper and was rejected outright, surfacing as a confusing AI 'invalid changes' error unrelated to what the user actually asked for.
fix: Added MAX_WIDTH_NAMED_SCALE and set UTILITY_FAMILIES["max-w"] = SIZING_SCALE | MAX_WIDTH_NAMED_SCALE. Deliberately left w/min-w/h/min-h/max-h on the numeric scale only, since the named scale is a max-w-specific Tailwind convention (w-4xl is not a real Tailwind class).

title: A user-reported AI rejection screenshot can have a misleading apparent cause - always check the server log for the real error string
cause: A screenshot showing 'La IA propuso cambios no válidos' for a YouTube-embed instruction looked like an iframe-rejection bug at a glance, but the actual server log (apps/ai_assistant/views.py's logger.warning) showed the real cause was 'disallowed Tailwind class: max-w-4xl' - a completely unrelated Tailwind allowlist gap the model happened to hit in the same generation attempt. Only after fixing that and re-running the exact original instruction did the real second cause (iframe fully forbidden) surface.
fix: Never fix the surface-level guess from a screenshot alone. Reproduce the exact instruction against a real server and read the structured log line the view already emits (user id + exact rejection reason) before writing any fix.

title: iframe embeds enabled for YouTube/Vimeo only, restricted by src prefix allowlist
cause: iframe was in sanitize.py's FORBIDDEN_TAGS entirely (security: arbitrary iframe src on a now-publicly-published page is a clickjacking/phishing vector), which silently blocked the common, legitimate request to embed a YouTube video with no clear error message to the end user.
fix: Removed iframe from FORBIDDEN_TAGS but added a tag-specific check in sanitize_node: iframe's src attribute must start with one of IFRAME_SRC_ALLOWED_PREFIXES (youtube.com/embed/, youtube-nocookie.com/embed/, player.vimeo.com/video/). Also updated the AI system prompt (prompts.py) to convert youtube watch URLs to embed URLs and to use aspect-video + absolute inset-0 w-full h-full instead of an arbitrary pb-[56.25%] padding-hack, which the model tried first and which the Tailwind allowlist correctly rejects (no arbitrary values supported).

title: Server-side iframe allowlist fix alone doesn't make embeds visible - CSP and client-side renderer have their own separate copies
cause: After fixing apps/ai_assistant/sanitize.py to allow YouTube/Vimeo iframe src, the user still couldn't see the embedded video in the editor preview. Two more, independent blockers existed: (1) the CSP header (frame-src 'self' in both config/settings/development.py and production.py) silently blocked the nested cross-origin frame in the browser with no visible error unless checking console/network; (2) static/editor/editor-core.js's own client-side renderNode() has a SEPARATE, hand-maintained forbiddenTags set (historically kept in sync manually with sanitize.py, per CLAUDE.md's note not to refactor this file) that dropped <iframe> unconditionally regardless of src.
fix: Any tag/attribute allowlist change touching client-visible rendering must be checked in THREE places for this project: apps/ai_assistant/sanitize.py (server validation), static/editor/editor-core.js's renderNode (client preview), and the CSP frame-src/img-src/etc directives (config/settings/development.py + production.py) - a fix in only one silently fails downstream with no clear error.

title: Sandbox restrictions on an iframe cascade to nested iframes - allow-same-origin alone is not enough for embedded video players
error_message: An error occurred. Unable to execute JavaScript.
cause: templates/editor/editor.html's #previewFrame had sandbox="allow-same-origin" only. Sandbox flags apply to the whole nested browsing-context tree: a nested <iframe> (the YouTube/Vimeo embed) cannot have MORE permissions than its ancestor's sandbox grants, regardless of its own attributes. Without allow-scripts on the outer preview frame, the nested YouTube player iframe loaded but couldn't execute its own JS, showing YouTube's generic error page instead of the video.
fix: Added allow-scripts to #previewFrame's sandbox attribute (sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts"). Safe here because all content inside the preview is already sanitized server-side before reaching state (no <script> tags, no on* handlers, no javascript: URLs allowed by sanitize.py) - allow-scripts only enables scripts that already passed that validation, it doesn't relax the sanitize.py allowlist itself.

title: YouTube embed Error 153 reproduced even from a real published page (not srcdoc) - environment/origin issue, not app code
error_message: Error 153 Error de configuración del reproductor de video
cause: After fixing CSP, editor-core.js's tag allowlist, and the preview iframe's sandbox, a live Playwright verification against BOTH the editor preview (srcdoc) and the actual published public page (a real, non-srcdoc document) still showed YouTube's own "Error 153" for two different, normally-fully-embeddable video IDs. Since the error reproduces even on a real served document, it rules out anything srcdoc/sandbox/CSP-specific in this codebase. This matches a well-known YouTube embed quirk: the embed verification/referrer check is known to reject 127.0.0.1/localhost-style origins in ways it wouldn't for a real registered domain.
fix: Not a code fix - flagged as an environment/domain limitation, not a maqueta bug. All three real fixes in this project (sanitize.py allowlist, CSP frame-src, editor-core.js renderNode, previewFrame sandbox) were independently confirmed working (no CSP violation, no "Unable to execute JavaScript", the iframe's own JS executes) - the remaining Error 153 must be re-checked against a real deployed domain, not localhost/127.0.0.1, before treating it as unresolved.

title: Confirmed via YouTube oEmbed API: Error 153 on localhost is an origin issue, not a video-embedding-disabled issue
error_message: Error 153 Video player configuration error
cause: User reproduced Error 153 in their own real browser at http://localhost:8000, matching the earlier sandbox reproduction. To rule out "this specific video has embedding disabled by its owner" (a common real cause of Error 153) as the explanation, queried YouTube's public oEmbed endpoint directly: curl "https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kAoSM_p3G5U&format=json" returned HTTP 200 with a valid embed <iframe> snippet - proving the video itself is embeddable and the owner has not restricted it.
fix: No code fix possible or needed - definitively confirmed environment-only limitation (localhost/127.0.0.1 origin), not a maqueta bug and not this-video-specific. Verify by testing on a real deployed domain before investigating further; curl the oEmbed endpoint for any future "Error 153" report to instantly rule out video-side restriction before assuming an app bug.

title: Deterministic content-insert presets (hero/features/cta/footer/product) predate the Tailwind migration and reference CSS classes that don't exist anywhere
cause: User reported "Insertar producto" added an ugly, unstyled card. Investigation found static/editor/editor-core.js's sectionPreset() (hero/features/text/image/cta/footer) and the old productCardNode() all use semantic class names (.hero, .container, .feature-grid, .cta-box, .product-card) with ZERO Tailwind utility classes - and no stylesheet anywhere in the project defines those semantic classes either. These are leftover pre-Tailwind-migration templates that were never updated when the rest of the project moved to Tailwind utilities.
fix: For the product card specifically, replaced the deterministic unstyled node with a call through the existing AI transform pipeline (which already generates real Tailwind classes) instead of hardcoding new Tailwind classes into productCardNode - user explicitly chose the AI-driven path over a quick deterministic Tailwind fix, given the tradeoff (instant/free/deterministic vs AI-authored/variable/costs a request) presented via AskUserQuestion. The hero/features/text/image/cta/footer presets are a still-open, separate finding - not fixed in this pass.

title: DRF SessionAuthentication runs its own CSRF check independent of Django's @csrf_exempt decorator
error_message: CSRF Failed: CSRF token missing.
cause: CheckoutView and StripeWebhookView both had @method_decorator(csrf_exempt, name="dispatch") and permission_classes=[AllowAny], intended to make them fully public/unauthenticated. But DRF's DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES includes SessionAuthentication, whose enforce_csrf() runs its OWN CSRF validation (calling Django's CsrfViewMiddleware machinery directly) whenever it successfully authenticates a request via a session cookie - completely independent of the view-level csrf_exempt decorator, which only defeats Django's CsrfViewMiddleware. A logged-in visitor (e.g. the template owner testing their own "Comprar" button, or anyone hitting the endpoint through the DRF browsable API while logged in) got a 403 'CSRF Failed: CSRF token missing.' despite the view being explicitly csrf_exempt. A truly logged-out anonymous buyer never hit this (no session to authenticate), which is why it looked fine in casual anonymous testing.
fix: Add authentication_classes = [] on any APIView that is permission_classes=[AllowAny] AND accepts POST/PUT/DELETE and is meant to be fully public - there is no reason to run session authentication (and therefore its CSRF check) on a request you don't intend to authenticate at all.

title: APIClient.force_authenticate bypasses DRF's real auth+CSRF pipeline - use client.login() to test CSRF-sensitive paths
cause: tests/conftest.py's api/anon_api fixtures use APIClient().force_authenticate(user), a DRF test helper that monkey-patches the request's authentication result directly, skipping SessionAuthentication (and therefore its enforce_csrf check) entirely. This meant the CheckoutView/StripeWebhookView CSRF-for-logged-in-sessions bug (see the paired learnings entry) was completely invisible to the existing test suite no matter how many tests were added using these fixtures.
fix: To regression-test any CSRF-sensitive behavior, use a real APIClient(enforce_csrf_checks=True) with client.login(username=..., password=...) (a real session, going through the actual auth pipeline) instead of force_authenticate. Verified the new test fails with 403 when the fix (authentication_classes=[]) is reverted, and passes with it in place - a real regression test, not just a happy-path check.

title: Fake payment provider marked sessions instantly-paid but nothing ever delivered the webhook that creates the Order, leaving buyers stuck forever
cause: FakePaymentProvider.create_checkout_session sets payment_status="paid" in its in-memory session dict at creation time, but the ONLY code path that ever creates an Order row is StripeWebhookView.post - and there is no real Stripe server in dev/test to ever call that webhook. SuccessView correctly refuses to fabricate an Order from its own retrieve_session fallback (by design, to avoid a false-positive purchase record), so with PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake (the default with no Stripe keys configured) every checkout got permanently stuck showing "Procesando tu pago... Todavia estamos confirmando tu pago" - reproduced live via a real logged-in browser session right after fixing the checkout CSRF bug (paired learnings entry).
fix: Extracted the webhook's order-creation logic into a shared _record_order_for_session(provider, session_id, product_id) function. CheckoutView now calls it directly, immediately after creating the session, but ONLY when isinstance(provider, FakePaymentProvider) - matching what the fake provider already pretends happened (instant successful payment). Real StripePaymentProvider checkouts are completely untouched and still require the actual signature-verified webhook; only the no-real-backend fake path gets this shortcut.

title: stripe.Webhook.construct_event returns a StripeObject, not a plain dict - isinstance(dict) checks silently fail
cause: The pre-existing StripeWebhookView code branched on isinstance(event, dict) to handle both a real Stripe event and FakePaymentProvider's json.loads(payload) plain dict with the same code path. This was NEVER actually exercised against a real signed Stripe event before this session's multi-gateway work (only FakePaymentProvider had ever been tested through the webhook view) - stripe.Webhook.construct_event returns a StripeObject (no .get(), doesn't match isinstance(x, dict)), so the isinstance branch silently always took the 'else' path, and that else path's own nested isinstance(session_obj, dict) check ALSO failed the same way, making client_reference_id extraction silently return None for every real Stripe webhook that would ever have fired in production.
fix: StripePaymentProvider.parse_webhook_event now calls event.to_dict() before returning, normalizing to a plain dict so every caller can use one code path (event.get(...)) regardless of whether the event came from Stripe's real SDK or a Fake provider's json.loads. Lesson: an isinstance(x, dict) branch that silently degrades instead of raising is a latent bug magnet - if a real test never exercises the 'else' path, it can silently never have worked.

title: Multi-gateway checkout architecture: buyer picks gateway, credentials are per-seller and encrypted at rest
fix: Implemented per PAYMENTS.md (deleted after this close-out, see specs/storefront/spec.md and CHANGELOG.md for the permanent record): 8 gateways (Stripe/Mercado Pago/PayPal/Braintree/Wompi/PayU/ePayco/Bold), each with a real + Fake* PaymentProvider pair behind GATEWAY_REGISTRY. PaymentGatewayConfig is owner-scoped (not global) with Fernet-encrypted credentials (apps/storefront/crypto.py, key derived from DJANGO_SECRET_KEY - rotating that key without a migration plan makes stored credentials unreadable, a real operational gotcha to remember). Order gained a gateway field; uniqueness on (gateway, gateway_session_id) not a global session id. GatewayWebhookView tries every enabled seller's credentials for a gateway until one verifies the signature, since a webhook payload carries no explicit seller identity. Confidence varies sharply by gateway - Stripe/Mercado Pago/Wompi/PayU/ePayco verification schemes are locally testable (HMAC/checksum, no network); PayPal/Braintree require mocking a real API/SDK call; Bold's real webhook spec was never confirmable (its docs are JS-rendered, this session's fetch tool only got navigation chrome) so BoldPaymentProvider.parse_webhook_event deliberately always raises rather than pretend to verify something unconfirmed.

title: URL shape changes for a checkout/buy button break already-published pages whose state was saved with the old form action baked in
error_message: Page not found (404) - Request URL: http://localhost:8000/comprar/6/
cause: The multi-gateway checkout migration changed /comprar/<id>/ to /comprar/<id>/<gateway>/, but a UserTemplate's product-card <form action=...> is a LITERAL value stored in state JSON at the time it was inserted (by the AI or otherwise) - it is never regenerated when a URL pattern changes server-side. An already-published page from before this session's multi-gateway work kept pointing at the old URL shape and 404'd for real, live-reproduced.
fix: Added a second URL (storefront:checkout-legacy) mapping the same CheckoutView with gateway=None, falling back to the seller's first enabled PaymentGatewayConfig (deterministic alphabetical order) instead of 404ing. Still 404s if the seller has nothing enabled at all - there's no gateway to fall back to in that case. General lesson: any URL-shape change for a route whose exact string gets baked into stored content (not just navigated to) needs an explicit backward-compat path, not just an updated URLconf.

title: No-gateway-configured checkout now delivers for free with a tracked $0 Order instead of 404ing
fix: User explicit decision (asked via AskUserQuestion, chose 'create a free Order' over 'no record at all'): CheckoutView._deliver_for_free() creates Order(gateway=Order.Gateway.NONE, amount_cents=0, status=PAID) and redirects straight to /gracias/ when the seller has zero PaymentGatewayConfig rows enabled - applies both to the new legacy no-gateway URL and any future path that resolves to 'nothing enabled'. SuccessView accepts gateway=none without trying to build a real PaymentProvider for it (GATEWAY_REGISTRY intentionally has no 'none' entry - it's an Order-only marker, not a payment gateway). Verified end-to-end via a real browser click on a published page.

title: Shared UI tokens eliminate page-level palette drift
cause: Server-rendered pages each owned near-duplicate token declarations and different font/background values, so visual changes could drift across editor, storefront, checkout, and auth surfaces.
fix: Extracted the canonical palette, typography, radius, and shadow variables into static/shared/tokens.css; linked it across all server-rendered UI surfaces; migrated local styles to canonical names; added structural pytest and real-browser Playwright coverage.

title: run-local.sh respects an existing PostgreSQL DATABASE_URL but does not start Docker
error_message: connection is bad: no error details available
cause: The existing .env set DATABASE_URL=postgres://editor:editor@localhost:5432/editor, while docker compose had no running db service. run-local.sh only creates .env when it is absent and never starts Docker, so manage.py migrate failed before runserver.
fix: Started docker compose up -d db, waited for PostgreSQL health, applied the pending migrations, and reran run-local.sh successfully; Django served /login/ with HTTP 200. Documented the prerequisite and the SQLite alternative in README.md and AGENTS.md.

title: run-local.sh starts local PostgreSQL before Django migrations
error_message: run-local.sh stopped at migrations when local PostgreSQL was not running
cause: PostgreSQL is the intended local database, but the bootstrap script previously assumed the compose db service had already been started manually.
fix: Made PostgreSQL the default in .env.example and taught run-local.sh to detect postgres:// or postgresql:// DATABASE_URL values, start docker compose up -d --wait db, and fail clearly when Docker or Compose is unavailable. Verified the Compose health-wait path and the existing Django /login/ endpoint returns HTTP 200.

title: run-local.sh detects an occupied development port
error_message: Error: That port is already in use.
cause: A previous Django runserver process was already listening on 0.0.0.0:8000; rerunning the bootstrap repeated setup and only failed when the second server tried to bind the same port.
fix: Added an early PORT validation and localhost TCP listener check to run-local.sh. It now explains the collision before dependency/CSS work and supports an explicit alternate port such as PORT=8001 ./run-local.sh. Verified the existing listener serves /login/ with HTTP 200 and the alternate-port startup succeeds.

title: Use ss for run-local.sh port detection in WSL
error_message: The Bash /dev/tcp probe could wait unexpectedly when an alternate port was unused in the WSL environment.
cause: A raw Bash TCP redirection is not a reliable fast availability probe in this local WSL setup, even though it detects an already-listening port.
fix: Replaced the /dev/tcp probe with an ss listening-socket check when ss is available; without ss, runserver remains the final fallback. Verified occupied-port detection exits quickly and PORT=8001 starts Django and serves /login/ with HTTP 200.

title: stop-local.sh stops Django without deleting PostgreSQL data
error_message: Error: That port is already in use.
cause: The local Django reloader leaves multiple runserver-related processes behind, so a repeat of run-local.sh needs to stop the whole matching process set rather than only one listener PID.
fix: Added executable stop-local.sh. By default it validates PORT, finds all run-local Django processes with pgrep, terminates them gracefully with a bounded wait, and leaves PostgreSQL running. The explicit --db option stops the compose db container without removing its volume. Verified the script stopped the active 8000 process tree, the --db cycle stopped and restarted PostgreSQL healthy, and no data volume was deleted.

title: Browser audit found editor dialog and checkout edge-state gaps
error_message: Escape did not close saveTemplateModal, paymentLinkModal, or imagePickerModal; /gracias/ measured 426px wide at a 390px viewport
cause: The editor Escape handler only considers elementModal and sectionModal, save-template.js has no Escape listener, and the checkout success card uses a fixed content-box width with padding. The audit also found missing focus trapping/restoration, an unnamed wizard textarea, silent storefront request failures, and incomplete wizard asset removal.
fix: No product fix was applied in this audit; documented the verified findings and acceptance order in UXUI.md, added backlog items 55-61, and linked the audit from README.md, AGENTS.md, and openspec/project.md.

title: Deterministic pytest gate uses the fake AI provider
error_message: tests/test_ai_transform.py::test_valid_request_returns_operations failed with KeyError: 'done' while .env used AI_PROVIDER=opencode_zen
cause: The live provider returned a Tailwind class rejected by the finite allowlist (shadow-[var(--color-primary)]/30), so the endpoint emitted invalid_operations instead of done; this is model-output variance, not a deterministic application failure.
fix: Ran AI_PROVIDER=fake uv run pytest; all 209 tests passed. Keep live-provider runs separate from the deterministic local gate.

title: Frontend UX implementation closes the audited interaction gaps
cause: The audit found editor preset rendering, modal keyboard behavior, mobile density, async feedback, wizard lifecycle, storefront edge states, and navigation gaps across separate frontend surfaces.
fix: Implemented allowlisted quick presets, centralized modal/focus behavior, responsive editor controls, shared feedback/navigation, wizard asset deletion and cancellation, fluid checkout/PayU/auth states, and browser regressions for the critical flows.

title: Payment credential validation must have no payment side effect
cause: Payment configuration needed a test-connection affordance, but using checkout creation for validation could create a session or charge and expose an unsafe operational path.
fix: Added an owner-scoped validation endpoint that checks required encrypted fields and initializes the real provider only; it reports missing fields or initialization failure without creating a checkout session.

title: Normalize malformed backlog CSV before appending audit records
error_message: CSV rows contained invalid quote escaping and an unquoted comma in a title.
cause: The historical BACKLOG.csv was not fully RFC-compliant, so a naive csv rewrite could misparse rows or truncate the file if opened before validation completed.
fix: Recovered the source atomically from HEAD, normalized only the malformed quoting/comma fields, validated every row against the header, and then appended the completed UX/UI records.

title: Add an explicit editor exit route
cause: The editor topbar exposed editing and save actions but no obvious way to leave the editor, forcing users to rely on browser navigation.
fix: Added an accessible Salir link beside the editor brand that returns to the authenticated template gallery and verified its visibility, label, destination, and responsive placement in Playwright.

title: Implement consent-gated anonymous analytics
error_message: The analytics TODO had no visitor/session telemetry or seller-facing heatmap.
cause: Public pages had no bounded, consent-aware event pipeline, and adding raw browser interaction data would risk coupling analytics to authentication or accepting personal/form values.
fix: Added apps.analytics with a separate HttpOnly pseudonymous visitor cookie, explicit consent, bounded pageview/heartbeat/click/pointer/page-exit events, owner-scoped metrics/session/heatmap APIs, 24x24 normalized aggregation, responsive dashboard, and purge_analytics retention. Validation rejects unsafe targets, out-of-range/non-finite coordinates, malformed payloads, and unknown sessions. Verified with 228 PostgreSQL pytest tests, 10 Playwright tests, Node tests, and Django checks.

title: Normalize legacy classes before AI context validation
error_message: Solicitud no válida (selected_node: disallowed Tailwind class: site-header).
cause: Pre-Tailwind editor pages intentionally retain semantic classes such as site-header and container for styles.rules backward compatibility, but TransformRequestSerializer validated the browser-provided selected-node context with the strict generated-Tailwind output allowlist.
fix: Added recursive AI-context normalization that removes only non-Tailwind class tokens before the shared structural/URL/attribute/depth checks, kept generated operation validation strict, changed the offline fake provider to emit bg-yellow-100, and added endpoint/allowlist regressions. Focused AI transform and Tailwind tests passed against PostgreSQL.

title: Ship server-backed template palette contract
error_message: Palette controls needed a bounded source of truth without breaking legacy templates or allowing unsafe CSS values.
cause: The editor and wizard previously had no shared palette contract, metadata validation, preset context, or accessible contrast feedback.
fix: Added the canonical four-role catalog and server validation, editor preset/custom/reset controls with atomic undo, wizard preset context, strict AI palette validation, legacy-safe rendering/export behavior, and regression coverage. Verified 244 PostgreSQL pytest tests, Node checks, Tailwind build, and 14 Playwright tests.

title: Do not infer palette provenance from matching colors
error_message: A legacy document without styles.palette could coincidentally contain the same four values as a current preset.
cause: The editor briefly treated matching legacy values as a selected preset, which would claim provenance that the stored JSON did not contain.
fix: Removed value-based preset inference; metadata now determines preset/AI provenance and metadata-free documents remain custom/legacy until the user explicitly changes the palette. Node checks and the 9-test editor Playwright suite passed afterward.

title: Synchronize capability records and archive completed TODO
error_message: The completed palette checklist remained duplicated across TODO.md, OpenSpec, UXUI.md, BACKLOG.csv, and learnings.jsonl, and openspec/project.md still contained a stale quick-insert warning.
cause: Implementation records had been updated incrementally, leaving duplicated historical checklists and one outdated gotcha after the frontend pass closed.
fix: Rewrote the palette OpenSpec as the authoritative implemented contract, synchronized editor/project/README/AGENTS/UXUI/CHANGELOG records, updated BACKLOG row 66 with documentation evidence, validated learnings.jsonl, and reduced TODO.md to deferred work plus source-of-truth links.

title: Document narrow YouTube/Vimeo iframe exception
error_message: The AI OpenSpec scenario described every iframe as forbidden even though the implementation supports approved YouTube/Vimeo embed prefixes.
cause: The security contract documented the default deny rule but omitted the deliberately narrow allowlist exception added for video embeds.
fix: Updated openspec/specs/ai-assistant/spec.md to require disallowed iframe sources to be rejected and to document the synchronized sanitizer, preview, and CSP embed-prefix checks.

title: Add owner-scoped reusable palettes
error_message: Reusable palettes were deferred because editor colors had no persistent owner-scoped catalog.
cause: Templates could store custom colors but users could not safely reuse them across documents or in the wizard.
fix: Added UserPalette persistence and migration, owner-scoped CRUD, canonical four-role validation, editor save/apply/delete controls, wizard resolution, and regression coverage. PostgreSQL tests and the editor browser flow passed.

title: Share editor and wizard SSE client
error_message: editor-ai.js and template-wizard.js duplicated stream parsing and reasoning-bubble behavior.
cause: Two AI surfaces had separate buffering, terminal-event, and live-reasoning implementations that could drift.
fix: Extracted static/shared/ai-stream.js with chunk buffering, final-block handling, terminal event collection, and surface callbacks; Node tests and the full Playwright suite passed after the hidden-control regression fix.

title: Keep native hidden controls hidden under component display rules
error_message: Playwright reported the palette delete button visible after deletion even though it had a hidden attribute.
cause: The editor button component declared its own display value, overriding the browser's default hidden presentation for the attribute-only control.
fix: Added an explicit [hidden] display:none!important rule to static/editor/editor.css and verified the owner save/reuse/delete palette flow in the official Playwright container.

title: Migrate frontend tooling from npm to pnpm
error_message: The project used npm install and npm run commands with package-lock.json across local, Docker, CI, and documentation workflows.
cause: The repository had no single pinned package-manager contract, so dependency installation and frontend commands were tied to npm.
fix: Pinned pnpm@10.33.2 in package.json, generated pnpm-lock.yaml, removed package-lock.json, switched local/Docker/CI commands to frozen pnpm installs and pnpm scripts, and synchronized the project documentation and backlog.

title: Add interactive local setup bootstrap
error_message: Developers had to discover and execute prerequisite, dependency, PostgreSQL, and migration commands manually before running run-local.sh.
cause: The repository had a canonical start script but no interactive prerequisite checker that could safely stop when a required installation was declined.
fix: Added executable setup.sh with confirmation-gated installers for uv, Python 3.12, Node 20 via nvm, pnpm 10.33.2 via Corepack, Docker/Compose, .env creation, dependency synchronization, Tailwind build, PostgreSQL readiness, and migrations; it never starts Django.
